scn.scribe_among_hostages.headline: {hostage.noun:scribe.indef} among the hostages
scn.scribe_among_hostages.body: {hostage.name} of {court.name} has spent the days since the taking writing on the cave wall with a burnt stick: the names of the dead at {a.place}, the year, the weather. Asked why, {hostage.subj} says someone should keep the record, and that nobody else here can read.
scn.scribe_among_hostages.because: You took {hostage.name} at {a.place} {a.years_ago:year} ago; {court.name} keeps a library, so its people are lettered.
scn.scribe_among_hostages.variant.scribe: {scribe.name} of {court.name} has covered the cave wall in charcoal: the names of the dead at {a.place}, the year, the weather. {scribe.subj} offers, without being asked, to keep your chronicle. Nobody else here can read.
scn.scribe_among_hostages.option.ignore: Let the writing stay on the wall
scn.scribe_among_hostages.reveal.keep: From now on the briefing tells you why, not only what, while this one lives.
scn.burned_library_scribes.headline: The scribes of {court.name}
scn.burned_library_scribes.body: {envoy.name} stands at the ledge with a satchel of ash. {a.years_ago:year} after you burned the library at {a.place}, {court.name} has no record of its own kings, and the young are taught from memory by the old. {envoy.noun:def} asks for what you took, or for someone to teach them letters again.
scn.burned_library_scribes.because: {court.name} lost its written memory at {a.place}; what it knows of you is now told, not read.
{sage.name}, the last {sage.noun} of {court.name}, has sent {envoy.name} with a satchel of ash from {a.place}. The hold has no record of its own kings now. {sage.noun:def} asks for the books you took, or for letters to be taught again.
scn.hero_at_dawn.headline: {hero.name} comes alone
scn.hero_at_dawn.body: {hero.name} of {court.name} stands on the lair's border at first light with a banner planted in the scree and no army behind it. {hero.subj} was a child at {a.place} when it burned, {a.years_ago:year} ago, and has sworn on that fire. The order waits a day's march back. This one wants it settled face to face.
scn.hero_at_dawn.because: The burning of {a.place} is written in {court.name}'s chronicle; {hero.name} is sworn to that memory.
scn.princess_returns.headline: A letter in a hand you taught
scn.princess_returns.body: A kestrel drops a letter on the ledge. {agent.name} writes from {court.name}'s throne that the priests have begun asking where the new {agent.noun} learned {agent.poss} craft, and that two of them have gone to the archive. {agent.subj} asks whether you would like the priests to find something, or nothing.
scn.princess_returns.because: You released {agent.name} {a.years_ago:year} ago, schooled in intrigue and touched by your magic; a devout court notices.
scn.princess_returns.option.gold: Send gold to the keeper of the archive
scn.inquisition_opens.headline: The inquisition of {court.name}
scn.inquisition_opens.body: {priest.name} has the court's mages in chains and its archive under seal. The charge is dark craft at the throne; the proof is thin and the fires are not. The mage guild's work has stopped. A court that burns its own scholars is weaker for a generation, and it knows who it blames.
scn.inquisition_opens.because: The secret you planted in {court.name} surfaced; a devout court with a weak crown answers with fire.
scn.inquisition_opens.variant.agent.body: {priest.name} has {agent.name}'s tutors in chains and the archive under seal. The charge is dark craft at the throne, and this time the proof is not thin. The mages' work has stopped. {agent.subj} has not been named yet.
scn.inquisition_opens.option.gift: Send {priest.noun:def} a relic to look at instead
scn.inquisition_opens.option.judge: Descend and spare the accused in judgement
scn.inquisition_opens.option.incite: Set the neighbour on them while they purge
scn.thief_with_the_cup.headline: The cup is on their table
scn.thief_with_the_cup.body: {cup.name:def} that lay under your left wing is now the centrepiece of {court.name}'s feast table, and the whole city has been quieter since. The thief has a street named after the walk back down. The city is rich, pleased with itself, and watching the sky more than it used to.
scn.thief_with_the_cup.because: A court that does not fear you sent a thief while you slept; it remembers the theft with pride.
scn.thief_with_the_cup.variant.thief.bod: {thief.name} came out of your mountain with {cup.name:def} and has not bought a drink since. {cup.subj} stands on {court.name}'s feast table and the city watches the sky more than it used to.
scn.thief_with_the_cup.option.gift: Send them exactly what else was taken
scn.thief_with_the_cup.reveal.gift: Generosity after a theft is remembered as a riddle; the court will send someone to ask what you meant.
scn.two_crowns.headline: Two crowns and {heir.noun:indef}
scn.two_crowns.body: {court.name} has no one for the throne but {heir.name}, asleep in your hoard, and {match.name} has a widowed queen and a long border. Both courts have written to each other; neither has written to you. A marriage would make one realm of two, and the mountain would stand between it and nothing.
scn.two_crowns.because: You hold {heir.name}; a marriage between the two courts needs {heir.obj}.
scn.two_crowns.variant.envoy.body: {envoy.name} of {match.name} has come to ask, very carefully, whether {heir.name} is well, and whether the mountain has views on marriage.
scn.pilgrims_in_winter.headline: Pilgrims at the foot of the mountain
scn.pilgrims_in_winter.body: Eleven of {court.name}'s faithful have come up the pass in the snow with a cart of {home.name}'s last apples and a child who will not stop looking at the cave. They do not ask for anything. They have come to be looked at.
scn.pilgrims_in_winter.because: {court.name} holds you in awe and the road from {home.name} is open.
scn.pilgrims_in_winter.variant.leader.bo: {leader.name} has led eleven of {court.name}'s faithful up the pass in the snow with a cart of {home.name}'s last apples. They do not ask for anything. They have come to be looked at, and {leader.subj} has brought a book to write down what they see.
scn.pilgrims_in_winter.variant.dread.bod: Eleven of {court.name}'s faithful have come up the pass in the snow. They walk slowly and keep the children at the back. They have brought the last apples from {home.name}, and they have not decided whether this is a gift or a tribute.
scn.pilgrims_in_winter.option.bless: Bless their fields instead of appearing
scn.pilgrims_in_winter.option.ignore: Let them wait and go home
scn.lich_crown_speaks.headline: {crown.name:def} speaks
scn.lich_crown_speaks.body: {crown.subj} waits until the cave is quiet. The living will always build cannon, {crown.subj} says, in the voice of the king who drowned wearing {crown.obj}. {crown.subj} can make you something cannon cannot reach. {crown.subj} does not say what that costs. {crown.subj} never does.
scn.lich_crown_speaks.because: An artifact with its own purpose has been in the hoard long enough to learn your fears.
scn.lich_crown_speaks.variant.armed.body: {crown.subj} waits until the cave is quiet. {armed.name} has cannon now, {crown.subj} says, in the voice of the king who drowned wearing {crown.obj}, and the living will always build more. {crown.subj} can make you something cannon cannot reach. {crown.subj} does not say what that costs.
scn.lich_crown_speaks.variant.dead.body: {crown.subj} waits until the cave is quiet. The dead of {dead.name} have priests now, {crown.subj} says, and the priests have a rite. {crown.subj} can make you something the living cannot kill. {crown.subj} does not say what you would be afterwards.
scn.lich_crown_speaks.option.gift: Give {crown.obj} to the dead and be rid of {crown.obj}
scn.door_in_the_temple.headline: A door in the temple of {temple.name}
scn.door_in_the_temple.body: The cult of {cult.name} has built a door in the temple at {temple.name} that opens onto nowhere yet. The priests say it opens for you. The neighbours say it opens for something else, and have sent soldiers to find out. Within two wakings it will open one way or the other, whether you are there or not.
scn.door_in_the_temple.because: Faith, magic and time have met in one court; a door is the shape they take.
scn.door_in_the_temple.variant.zealot.bo: The cult of {cult.name} has built a door at {temple.name} that opens onto nowhere yet. {zealot.name}'s soldiers are already in the valley below it with torches. Within two wakings it opens one way or the other, whether you are there or not.
scn.door_in_the_temple.option.consecrate: Consecrate the temple as your own
scn.door_in_the_temple.option.destroy: Break the altar and the door with it
scn.door_in_the_temple.option.defend: Hold the pass against the soldiers
scn.door_in_the_temple.reveal.ignore: If the door opens without you, something may come the other way.
scn.dwarves_ask_for_fire.headline: The dwarves ask for fire
scn.dwarves_ask_for_fire.body: {envoy.name} of {hold.name} has brought a block of the hold's best steel as a gift and a request written in the Book: the orcs of {foe.name} have the lower galleries, and the hold's forges cannot make a heat that holds them. The dwarves do not ask you to burn anyone. They ask how fire is made to stay.
scn.dwarves_ask_for_fire.because: {hold.name} is at war with {foe.name} and open enough to ask a dragon for craft.
scn.dwarves_ask_for_fire.option.teach: Teach their smiths the craft of lasting fire
scn.dwarves_ask_for_fire.option.burn: Burn the orcs out of the galleries yourself
scn.dwarves_ask_for_fire.reveal.teach: Dwarves who learn fire from a dragon will one day sell engines that reach the clouds.
scn.quiet_valley.headline: Nobody is looking at the mountain
scn.quiet_valley.body: Three wakings, three hooks left where they hung. In {court.name} the children are told the mountain has a dragon in it the way they are told the lake has a woman in it. A shepherd grazes goats on the lower slopes. The valley has stopped watching the sky, and it has stopped building things that point at it, too.
scn.quiet_valley.because: You have answered nothing for three wakings; what is not seen is not remembered.
scn.quiet_valley.variant.third.body: Three wakings, three hooks left where they hung. {court.name} tells its children the mountain has a dragon in it the way it tells them the lake has a woman in it. A shepherd grazes goats on your slopes. Nobody is building anything that points at the sky.
scn.quiet_valley.variant.late_era.body: Three wakings, three hooks left where they hung. {court.name} has stone walls and a clock tower now and does not look up at the mountain at all. Nobody is building anything that points at the sky. The engineers have other work.
scn.quiet_valley.option.show: Land in their square at noon
scn.quiet_valley.option.preach: Walk among them and start a rumour
scn.quiet_valley.reveal.ignore: A forgotten dragon's next act is read as a first act; the forgetting is also an opening.
scn.the_mountain.headline: The slopes are your shoulders
scn.the_mountain.body: You have not fitted through the cave mouth for a hundred years. Snow stays on your back between wakings now. Goats graze on your tail. If you slept the long sleep here, the valley would build on you and call the mountain by your name, and no engine they ever make would reach your heart.
scn.the_mountain.because: Might past a threshold and a long sleep make a dragon into a mountain.
scn.the_mountain.variant.settlers.body: You have not fitted through the cave mouth for a hundred years. {settlers.name} has a village on your lower slopes already; they think it is a hill. If you slept the long sleep here they would build a city on you and call the mountain by your name.
scn.the_mountain.option.terraform: Raise the ground around you and settle in
scn.the_mountain.option.demand: Demand that they come as pilgrims, not squatters
scn.the_mountain.option.sleep: Sleep the long sleep, here, now
scn.the_consort.headline: {willing.name} has followed you up the mountain
scn.the_consort.body: You walked {court.name}'s streets in a borrowed shape and {willing.name} walked with you, and knew, and came anyway. {willing.subj} is standing at the cave mouth now, with a travelling bag and the expression of someone who has already decided. Mortals age while you sleep. {willing.subj} knows that too.
scn.the_consort.because: You went among them in guise this waking; one of them saw through it and chose you.
scn.false_dragon.headline: {pretender.name} speaks for the mountain
scn.false_dragon.body: {pretender.name} of {court.name} has announced that the mountain speaks to {pretender.obj} alone, and has raised the tithe in its name. The shrine's offerings go to the palace now. The faithful are uneasy and quiet. The sky has not confirmed or denied anything, which {pretender.name} calls agreement.
scn.false_dragon.because: A long absence and a faithful court leave room for someone to hold your worship for you.
scn.false_dragon.option.preach: Walk the city and correct the story
scn.false_dragon.option.miracle: Answer the faithful with a miracle
scn.false_dragon.option.burn: Burn the palace that collects your tithe
scn.envoy_who_lies.headline: {envoy.name} brings news of a plot
scn.envoy_who_lies.body: {envoy.name} of {court.name} has climbed the pass to warn you: {rival.name} is forging engines to slay you and has sworn it at its altar. {court.name} asks only that you strike first, and offers forty gold a year in gratitude. {envoy.subj} does not meet your eye when naming the altar.
scn.envoy_who_lies.because: A court at war with a stronger neighbour has a reason to want you angry at it.
scn.envoy_who_lies.variant.keen_eyes.bod: {envoy.name} of {court.name} warns you that {rival.name} is forging engines to slay you. {envoy.noun:def.gen} eyes say otherwise: {rival.name} has no slayers and no engines. {court.name} is losing a war and would like you to win it.
scn.envoy_who_lies.variant.dread.body: {envoy.name} of {court.name} has climbed the pass and stands as far from the cave as the ledge allows. {rival.name} is forging engines to slay you, {envoy.noun:def} says, too quickly, and {court.name} would pay forty gold a year to see them burned first. The hands shake. The story does not.
scn.envoy_who_lies.option.swear: Swear to burn the rival for forty a year
scn.refugee_column.headline: A column on the pass road
scn.refugee_column.body: Two hundred of {lost.name}'s people are on the road below with carts and no soldiers. {taker.name} has their valley. They have come to the mountain because the mountain is the one thing in the valley {taker.name} is afraid of. They will plant anywhere you point.
scn.refugee_column.because: {lost.name} lost its land to {taker.name} and holds you in some awe; the mountain is the last door.
scn.refugee_column.variant.elder.body: Two hundred of {lost.name}'s people are on the road below, led by {elder.name}, who remembers when you last flew over {lost.name} and has been telling the children about it for a week to keep them walking. They will plant anywhere you point.
scn.refugee_column.variant.orc_taker.bod: Two hundred of {lost.name}'s people are on the road below with carts and no soldiers. The orcs of {taker.name} have their valley and, by the smoke, their harvest. They have come to the mountain because the orcs will not. They will plant anywhere you point.
scn.refugee_column.option.defend: Take their valley back for them
scn.refugee_column.option.skip: Do nothing; they will move on
scn.prophet_with_the_prophecy.headline: {prophet.name} has read the lines
scn.prophet_with_the_prophecy.body: {prophet.name} of {court.name} has walked up the mountain with the book open. {prophet.subj} has read the prophecy forty times and believes it is about you and about now. {prophet.subj} wants to tell you what the four peoples and the house of stone mean, and what {court.name} must build. {prophet.subj} also wants to be the one living voice.
scn.prophet_with_the_prophecy.because: {court.name} holds the prophecy and holds you in awe; a devout priest draws the obvious conclusion.
scn.prophet_with_the_prophecy.reveal.rec: {prophet.noun:def.gen} reading of the four conditions is shown on the Endings page from now on, with {prophet.poss} bias.
scn.kin_of_a_hostage.headline: {kin.name} has come for {hostage.name}
scn.kin_of_a_hostage.body: {kin.name} of {court.name} has come up the pass alone, which took some courage, and stands at the ledge asking to see {hostage.name}. {kin.subj} has brought a ransom and a speech. The speech is about how long {hostage.name} has been gone and how the court needs {hostage.noun:heir.def}. The ransom is less than you would have asked.
scn.kin_of_a_hostage.because: {kin.name} knows where you are and is not too afraid to come.
scn.kin_of_a_hostage.variant.bold.body: {kin.name} of {court.name} has come up the pass alone and stands at the ledge demanding, not asking, to see {hostage.name}. {kin.subj} has brought a ransom and no speech. The ransom is fair.
scn.kin_of_a_hostage.variant.awe.body: {kin.name} of {court.name} has come up the pass with a small offering for the shrine and a larger one for you, and asks to see {hostage.name} before anything is said about ransom. {kin.subj} kneels at the ledge, which {hostage.name} finds very funny.
scn.slayer_at_the_ledge.headline: {slayer.name} asks for single combat
scn.slayer_at_the_ledge.body: {slayer.name} of the order at {court.name} has walked up to the ledge in full plate with a sealed letter from the grandmaster and a challenge: fight here, now, one against one, and whoever lives keeps the mountain. {slayer.subj} has a burn scar down one side that did not come from you. Not yet.
scn.slayer_at_the_ledge.because: An order with a grievance and your exact location sends its best before it sends everyone.
scn.slayer_at_the_ledge.variant.order_re: {slayer.name} of the order at {court.name} has walked up to the ledge in full plate while the rest of the order waits a day's march back, ready. The challenge is single combat, here, now. If you refuse, {slayer.subj} says, they all come, and soon.
{slayer.name} of the order at {court.name} has walked up to the ledge in full plate and has clearly been told you are hurt. The challenge is single combat, here, now. {slayer.subj} looks at the way you hold your wing and smiles.
scn.slayer_at_the_ledge.option.haunt: Fill {slayer.noun:def.gen} night with what fire does
scn.slayer_at_the_ledge.option.reveal: Tell {slayer.noun:def} what the order plans for {slayer.obj}
scn.slayer_at_the_ledge.option.ignore: Leave the challenge on the ledge
scn.the_walls_went_up.headline: {court.name} has walls now
scn.the_walls_went_up.body: Where you burned {a.place} {a.years_ago:year} ago there is stone to the height of a house and towers at the corners, each with a slot cut for a bolt-thrower that does not exist yet. The quarry is three valleys away. They have spent a generation's wealth on this, and they will tell you so if you land.
scn.the_walls_went_up.because: A court that remembers a burning and has reached the age of castles builds against the sky.
scn.the_walls_went_up.variant.mason.body: {mason.name} of {court.name} designed the new walls at {a.place}, stone to the height of a house with a slot in every tower for a bolt-thrower that does not exist yet. {mason.subj} has written a treatise on dragon fire. It is mostly wrong.
scn.the_walls_went_up.option.walls: Burn the walls while they are new
scn.the_walls_went_up.option.demand: Demand they tear the towers down
scn.the_walls_went_up.option.show: Land inside the walls, in the square
scn.the_walls_went_up.reveal.ignore: Walls that stand for an age become a court's pride; pride founds slayer orders.
scn.the_gold_you_took.headline: An empty treasury and a full neighbour
scn.the_gold_you_took.body: The gold you took from {court.name} {a.years_ago:year} ago was the gold that paid its soldiers. The soldiers have gone to {rival.name}, which pays. {court.name} is now a city that cannot defend its own gates, and {rival.name} has noticed.
scn.the_gold_you_took.because: You took {a.size} of {court.name}'s wealth; a poor court cannot keep an army.
scn.the_gold_you_took.option.give: Return a third of it, quietly
scn.the_gold_you_took.option.ignore: A poor court is a quiet court
scn.the_army_you_broke.headline: A road of cairns
scn.the_army_you_broke.body: The road from {a.place} to {court.name}'s capital is lined with cairns now, one for each company you burned on the march. {widow.name} rules a court of widows and boys. The boys are training with spears in the square, and the drill-master was there that day.
scn.the_army_you_broke.because: You killed {a.size} of {court.name}'s army at {a.place}; a martial court remembers its dead in stone.
scn.the_army_you_broke.variant.general.b: {general.name} survived the march you burned at {a.place} and has not stopped talking about it. The road is lined with cairns. The boys drilling in {court.name}'s square call {general.obj} teacher.
scn.the_army_you_broke.option.crush: Finish the garrison before the boys grow
scn.the_city_you_saved.headline: A feast day in {court.name}
scn.the_city_you_saved.body: {court.name} keeps the day you broke the siege at {a.place} as a holiday now. {ruler.name} has had your likeness carved over the gate, a little too thin and with too many teeth. Children leave bread on the walls. The priests are arguing about whether bread is enough.
scn.the_city_you_saved.because: You defended {court.name} {a.years_ago:year} ago; a saved city turns gratitude into ritual within a generation.
{court.name} keeps the day you broke {attacker.name}'s siege at {a.place} as a holiday. {ruler.name} has had your likeness carved over the gate, too thin and with too many teeth. {attacker.name} keeps the day too, differently.
scn.the_city_you_saved.option.show: Fly over the feast at noon
scn.the_city_you_saved.option.demand: Ask for tribute in place of bread
scn.the_oath_they_remember.headline: The oath is in the book
scn.the_oath_they_remember.body: {heir.name} of {court.name} has read the oath {heir.subj} inherited: tribute to the mountain, sworn {a.years_ago:year} ago by a terrified ancestor. The book also records why. {heir.name} is not terrified. The tribute has arrived this year, exactly, with a note asking whether the mountain is still there.
scn.the_oath_they_remember.because: A written oath outlives the dread that made it; {heir.noun:def} keeps the letter and tests the spirit.
scn.the_oath_they_remember.option.releas: Release them from the oath, with grace
scn.the_oath_they_remember.option.ignore: Take the gold and say nothing
scn.the_pupils.headline: What the pupils did with it
scn.the_pupils.body: You taught {court.name} {a.years_ago:year} ago. {sage.name} runs a school now where that lesson is the first week. The second week is about dragons. The school has a tower, the tower has a telescope, and the telescope points at the mountain every clear night.
scn.the_pupils.because: A court you taught teaches itself; what it learns next is not yours to choose.
scn.the_one_you_spared.headline: {spared.name} rules now
scn.the_one_you_spared.body: You judged {spared.name} and let {spared.obj} live, in front of the whole square, {a.years_ago:year} ago. {spared.name} rules {court.name} now and has never once mentioned it in public. In private, every envoy who leaves for the mountain is briefed by {spared.name} personally.
scn.the_one_you_spared.because: A public mercy left {spared.name} owing you, and unable to say so.
You judged {spared.name} and let {spared.obj} live, in front of the whole square. {spared.name} rules {court.name} now and has never forgiven the square for watching. Every envoy who leaves for the mountain is briefed personally, and the brief is not kind.
scn.the_one_you_spared.option.broker: Use the debt: broker a peace through {spared.obj}
scn.the_road_of_your_shadow.headline: They saw you pass
scn.the_road_of_your_shadow.body: You flew low over {court.name} {a.years_ago:year} ago and burned nothing. The road your shadow crossed is called the dragon's road now and the farmers along it leave the first sheaf at the milestone. Nobody has asked you for anything. They might, if you landed.
scn.the_road_of_your_shadow.because: A dragon seen and not feared becomes a story the fields tell.
scn.the_road_of_your_shadow.variant.chil: You flew low over {court.name} and burned nothing. {child.name}, {child.noun:def}, was on the road and has drawn you on every wall of the palace since. The farmers leave the first sheaf at the milestone where your shadow crossed.
scn.the_road_of_your_shadow.variant.late: You flew low over {court.name} and burned nothing. The astronomers logged the hour and the heading. The farmers leave the first sheaf at the milestone anyway; the astronomers find this embarrassing.
scn.the_road_of_your_shadow.option.bless: Bless the fields along the road
scn.the_heir_who_grew_up_here.headline: {hostage.name} asks to go home a ruler
scn.the_heir_who_grew_up_here.body: {hostage.name} was a child when you took {hostage.obj} from {court.name} {a.years_ago:year} ago, and is not a child now. {regent.name} rules in {hostage.name}'s name and would rather not stop. {hostage.name} asks for the throne, and for you to be seen at the coronation, and says it as someone who knows what the request costs you.
scn.the_heir_who_grew_up_here.because: {hostage.name}, raised in the hoard, comes of age with a claim, a debt and a view of the valley from above.
scn.the_heir_who_grew_up_here.option.rel: Send {hostage.obj} home with your sign on {hostage.obj}
scn.the_heir_who_grew_up_here.option.spo: Back the claim with a war
scn.the_dead_you_raised.headline: The dead have built a chapel
scn.the_dead_you_raised.body: The host you raised at {a.place} did not fall when the war ended. It stayed, and the fen it holds has a chapel in it now, roofed with shields. {living.name} says the dead are praying. Nobody has gone close enough to hear to whom.
scn.the_dead_you_raised.because: You raised the dead {a.years_ago:year} ago; what you raise and do not dismiss finds its own reasons.
scn.the_dead_you_raised.variant.priest.b: The host you raised at {a.place} has {priest.noun:indef} now, {priest.name}, who was alive when you raised the others and is not quite alive now. {living.name} says the dead are praying and that the prayers name the mountain.
scn.the_dead_you_raised.option.defend: Stand with the living against them
